user.title: Velador
user.description: Velador watches every loaded integration and revives the ones that die silently (config entry loaded, entities unavailable). No configuration needed — tune sensitivity later in Options.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single instance is possible.

data.min_entities: Minimum entities for an integration to be watched
data.strikes: Consecutive failed scans before declaring zombie
data.cooldown_hours: Hours between reload attempts of the same integration
data.grace_minutes: Grace minutes after Home Assistant starts
data.stale_minutes: Minutes without reporting to declare stale
data.canary_entities: Canaries: critical entities that heal their integration when they die
data.canary_minutes: Minutes a canary must be unavailable before healing
data.wan_entity: WAN connectivity entity (optional: no internet, no cloud heals wasted)
data.device_zombie_hours: Device-zombie hours (0 = off): flag devices with ALL entities dead longer than this
data.auto_stale: Auto-detect stale sensors (learns each sensor's own cadence)

zombie.title: Zombie integration: {title}
zombie.description: The integration **{title}** ({domain}) reports as loaded but {dead} of {total} of its entities are unavailable. Velador will try to reload it automatically.

confirm.title: Revive now
confirm.description: Reset strikes and cooldowns and reload the integration right now. Use this after fixing the physical cause (reconnected the device, renewed credentials, power is back).

stale.title: Stale sensor: {entity_id}
stale.description: **{entity_id}** has not reported for {minutes} minutes and still shows {state} as if it were current. A frozen sensor's last value is a lie — check the device, its battery or its mesh.

reauth.title: Re-authentication pending: {title}
reauth.description: The integration **{title}** ({domain}) has an open re-authentication flow — reloading will NOT cure it, it needs credentials. Velador will not waste reloads on it. Resolve the reauth in Settings → Devices & Services.

storm.title: Storm: {count} integrations died together
storm.description: {count} integrations became zombies in the same scan ({titles}) at {time}. This is likely a power outage or network drop, not {count} independent failures. Velador is reloading them sequentially, spaced out, so they do not stampede a router that just rebooted.

flapping.title: Unstable integration: {title}
flapping.description: The integration **{title}** ({domain}) has been revived {count} times in the last {hours} hours. Reloading is masking a physical problem — check power, cabling, radio coverage or batteries. Auto-heal is suppressed until it stays stable.

device_zombies.title: {count} device(s) completely dead
device_zombies.description: Devices with ALL their entities unavailable for more than {hours} hours: {names}. The integration ratio never sees this (3 dead entities out of 40 is 7%). Check power, switch, battery or mesh for each device.

auto_stale.title: Sensor gone quiet: {entity_id}
auto_stale.description: **{entity_id}** has not reported for {minutes} minutes, but it normally reports every {cadence} minutes. Nothing marked it unavailable — it just went silent. Check the device, its battery or its mesh.

restart_diff.title: {count} integration(s) did not come back after the restart
restart_diff.description:
These were healthy before the last restart and are not now: {entries}.

Nothing else will tell you this: a config entry that quietly fails to return after a reboot looks the same as one that was never there.

restart_diff_update.title: {count} integration(s) did not survive the Home Assistant update
restart_diff_update.description:
Home Assistant went from **{ha_antes}** to **{ha_ahora}**, and these were healthy before and are not now: {entries}.

A version change plus integrations that don't come back usually means a breaking change — check their release notes before assuming hardware.
